title: Enterprise onboarding & integration playbook
author: Priya Narang
body:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s recommended process, checklists, and runbooks for enterprise onboarding, technical integration, escalation handling, known issues & workarounds, and recurring health check / QBR materials. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and Eng stakeholders who own onboarding and post-sale adoption for enterprise customers.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-prod-request to <= 10 business days for standard integrations.
- Surface and remediate integration blockers within 72 hours of identification.
- Provide clear escalation paths that resolve sev1/sev2 issues within SLOs (see SLA table).

Scope:
- Applies to: Dedicated, Hosted API, and Private (VPC/on-prem) customer onboarding for enterprise contracts.
- Excludes: Proof-of-concept pilots run by developer trials (use the "quickstart" template instead).

Owner and contacts:
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (owner: Priya Narang)
- Primary SE contact: Ethan Park (se-technical-lead@redwood.com)
- Support triage lead: Monica Ruiz (support-lead@redwood.com)
- Eng on-call alias (runtime): eng-serving-runtime-oncall@redwood.com

Roles & responsibilities:
- Customer Success (CS): overall onboarding project management, business QBR coordination, adoption metrics.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): integration design, sample prompts, test harness, run successful end-to-end validation.
- Support: first-line triage of issues; create and update tickets; own severity assessment.
- Engineering (Runtime / Infra): bug fixes, performance tuning, capacity adjustments.
- Customer: provide network info, API usage patterns, sample data, and test accounts.

Onboarding phases (high level):
1) Discovery (Day 0-2)
   - Deliverables: kickoff agenda, success criteria, technical contact list.
   - Activities: gather business context, expected QPS, latency targets, data residency requirements, compliance needs.
2) Design & Network Prep (Day 2-5)
   - Deliverables: integration design doc, firewall/IP allowlist, cert/key exchange plan.
   - Activities: define private deployment vs hosted, determine egress/ingress rules.
3) Integration & Validation (Day 5-10)
   - Deliverables: working API key, test harness, validated requests, sample workload run.
   - Activities: implement auth, verify CORS/network, run smoke tests, validate model outputs vs acceptance criteria.
4) Launch & Handoff (Day 10+)
   - Deliverables: runbook handoff, QBR invite, monitoring dashboards, support escalation paths.
   - Activities: final capacity commit, enable production keys, turn over runbooks to CS and Support.

Minimum onboarding checklist (must be completed before production keys are issued):
- [ ] Signed contract and SSO/SCIM provisioning plan.
- [ ] Network connectivity validated (allowlist configured or VPC peering established).
- [ ] API authentication method tested (API key / mTLS / IAM).
- [ ] Baseline test harness run (10-100 representative requests, recorded traces).
- [ ] Latency/throughput baseline recorded in Console.
- [ ] Security scan (if private/on-prem) completed and evidence attached.
- [ ] QBR cadence scheduled and attendees confirmed.

Integration guide (technical summary) — quick-reference:
- API endpoints: Hosted: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; Dedicated: customer-specific host (see onboarding doc); Private: internal hostname per deployment.
- Auth: API keys (Bearer), optional mTLS for Private deployments, and IAM-based tokens for cloud marketplaces.

Sample curl (hosted):
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","input":"Say hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Network & firewall requirements (table):
- Purpose: Allow outbound to Redwood control plane and runtime.
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS)
- IPs: For hosted customers, provide allowlist CIDR block per region (see related_pages link to infra doc)
- TLS: TLS1.2+; certificates validated via public CA (private deployments may use customer CA)

Acceptance tests (examples):
- Functional: model returns expected structure for canonical prompts (attach prompt set).
- Performance: 95th p50/p95 token latency within SLO for the selected plan.
- Cost/Usage: estimated token cost <= negotiated threshold for trial workload.

Common integration failure modes & workarounds:
- Authentication failures (401/403):
  - Symptom: immediate 401 on every request.
  - Troubleshooting: verify API key, check key scope and expiry, ensure header is exactly "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>".
  - Workaround: Generate a short-lived test key and verify; if using mTLS, confirm client cert chain.
- DNS/name resolution errors:
  - Symptom: cannot resolve runtime host in private deployment.
  - Troubleshooting: check internal DNS entries, ensure kube-dns/consul entries propagated.
  - Workaround: Add host entry temporarily for validation, then fix DNS as long-term.
- Large payloads hitting rate limits:
  - Symptom: 429 returned for large-batch requests.
  - Troubleshooting: inspect rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining).
  - Workaround: reduce batch size or apply batching configuration from Redwood Optimize; request quota increase via Support.
- Model quality regressions after rollout:
  - Symptom: increased semantic errors or customer complaints after model version change.
  - Troubleshooting: compare evaluation prompt-set results against baseline; check rollout percentage.
  - Workaround: Initiate automatic rollback to prior model variant; open regression ticket to Applied ML team.

Escalation playbook (severity definitions & steps):
- Severity matrix:
  - SEV1: Production outage or critical feature broken causing customer revenue loss. Target response: 15m ack, 4h resolution target.
  - SEV2: Major feature impacted, significant degradation. Target response: 30m ack, 24h resolution target.
  - SEV3: Non-critical bug, cosmetic, or minor impact. Target response: 4h ack, next-sprint fix.

Escalation steps (ordered):
1) Triage (Support): assign severity, gather logs/traces, validate reproducibility, attempt immediate mitigations (restart, route fallback).
2) Notify CS & SE: update customer and internal stakeholders within 30 minutes (SEV1) or 4 hours (SEV2).
3) Open engineering incident (if SEV1/SEV2): link ticket to internal incident channel, engage runtime oncall, and create incident doc.
4) Mitigation & fix: Eng provides fix or workaround; SE tests and pushes canary; CS communicates status to customer.
5) Postmortem: For SEV1/SEV2, full postmortem required within 72 hours and follow-up actions tracked.

Support process & SLAs (summary table):
- Support tiers: Standard (email/web), Priority (24/7 phone + faster SLAs)
- Response targets by tier and severity:
  - Priority SEV1: 15m; SEV2: 30m; SEV3: 2h
  - Standard SEV1: 1h; SEV2: 4h; SEV3: 8h
- Bug fix SLAs depend on severity and contract (refer to customer contract).

Ticket triage checklist (Support):
1) Confirm customer identity and subscription.
2) Reproduce issue with logs and request IDs.
3) Establish impact and assign severity.
4) If SEV1/SEV2, follow Escalation steps and open incident channel.

Known issues & documented workarounds (operational shortlist):
- Issue: Intermittent KV cache mismatch causing repeated tokenization differences.
  - Workaround: Clear prefix cache for customer session via admin API; schedule model cache rotation.
- Issue: Gradual throughput drop on 8xA100 pools during heavy long-context workloads.
  - Workaround: Switch to short-context optimized instance pool or apply adaptive batching policy in Console.
- Issue: SCIM provisioning fails with certain Okta tenant configs.
  - Workaround: Collect Okta debug logs, use manual invite flow for initial users, and raise support ticket with identity engineering.

Health checks & QBR materials (what to prepare each quarter):
- Required dashboards / metrics:
  - Adoption: daily active API keys, percent of prod traffic vs test.
  - Reliability: error rate (5xx%) by route, availability by region, mean-time-to-first-byte.
  - Performance: p50/p95 token latency, throughput (tokens/s).
  - Cost: tokens per successful request, estimated monthly token spend vs forecast.
  - Quality: top 10 prompt validation failures, regression alert history.

Sample QBR agenda (45-60 min):
1) Introductions & agenda (5m)
2) Business outcomes & adoption highlights (10m)
3) Reliability/performance review (10m)
4) Quality & model evaluation results (10m)
5) Roadmap & next steps (10m)
6) Action items & owners (5m)

QBR collateral checklist:
- Export of Console dashboard (last 90 days)
- Top failed prompt set with examples and suggested mitigations
- Cost optimization opportunities (batching, quantization recommendations)
- Open escalations and their status

Runbook handover checklist (to Support & Customer):
- Detailed API key rotation steps and contact list.
- How to access traces & request logs in Console.
- Who to call for SEV1 after hours (priority customers): phone number & escalation alias.
- Post-deployment verification steps for new model rollouts.

Retention & documentation rules:
- All incident pages must be created in confluence/oncall-and-incident-response and linked to the ticket.
- Onboarding artifacts (network diagrams, signed evidence, scan results) must be attached to the customer record in the CS CRM and archived in Confluence.

Appendix A — Useful commands & API snippets:
- Admin: invalidate cache for customer_id via admin API
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_KEY>" https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/customers/<customer_id>/cache/invalidate

- Retrieve recent traces (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/traces?customer_id=<id>&since=24h

Related pages and templates:
- Enterprise onboarding checklist template: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding-and-support-playbook-2026
- QBR presentation template: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/qbr-and-health-checks-onboarding-playbook-2025
